articles.title: DEVELOPMENT OF INLAND WATERWAYS AND RELATED PROJECTS
articles.description: Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways DEVELOPMENT OF INLAND WATERWAYS AND RELATED PROJECTS Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi The Government of India has embarked upon a transformational drive to promote Inland Water Transport (IWT) as a key pillar of India's multimodal transport system under Maritime India Vision 2030 and Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047. The primary objective encompasses creating world-class waterway infrastructure through fairway development, multimodal terminals, community jetties, river cruise terminals, regional centres of excellence, digital navigation tools, and green vessel technologies, coupled with seamless integration under the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan. The development and regulation of National Waterways (NWs) are spearheaded by the Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), an autonomous organization under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. To improve the Ease of Doing Business and simplify approvals, IWAI has introduced an array of digital reforms: PANI: Portal for Asset and Navigation Information to facilitate seamless navigation planning. Jalyan & Navic Portal: A centralized database and digital portal developed on the lines of 'Vahan' and 'Sarathi' for nationwide online registration of vessels and crew, enabling accurate tracking and strategic planning. CAR-D: Cargo Data Portal for real-time tracking and logistics data integration. Jal Samriddhi Portal: Dedicated portal supporting commercial and operational activities across National Waterways. Digital Charts and Hydrographic Surveys: Modern hydrographic charts provided digitally to Mariners for enhanced safety. These infrastructure, digital, and policy reforms have resulted in the operationalization of 32 National Waterways across the country, laying the foundation for a technology-driven, sustainable, and globally competitive IWT ecosystem that reduces logistics costs, promotes green mobility, and accelerates inclusive economic growth. LOGISTICS EFFICIENCY & ENVIRONMENTAL COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS Inland Water Transport serves as an economic and environmentally friendly alternate mode of transport to Rail and Road, significantly reducing congestion on existing transport networks. Economic Freight Cost Comparison (2014 Price Baseline) Inland Water Transport (IWT): Rs. 1.06 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm) Railways: Rs. 1.36 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm) Highways (Road): Rs. 2.50 per Ton-Kilometer (TKm) (Source: Ministry of Railways, TTSS, and IWAI) Environmental Impact & Emission Analysis Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Emissions: IWT emits 0.0006 Rs/TKm, on par with Railways (0.0006 Rs/TKm) and significantly lower than Roadways (0.0031 Rs/TKm). Air Pollution Costs: IWT accounts for 0.03 Rs/TKm, compared to 0.0366 Rs/TKm for Railways and 0.202 Rs/TKm for Roadways. Noise, Soil & Water Pollution: IWT has negligible impact on noise, soil, and water pollution, whereas Road transport incurs 0.0032 Rs/TKm (noise) and 0.005 Rs/TKm (soil/water). (Source: 12th Five Year Plan, Planning Commission TTS Study, PIANC) POLICY MEASURES & SECTORAL REFORMS Jalvahak Scheme: A scheme providing 35% financial incentive to cargo owners and scheduled operators for cargo movement on NW-1, NW-2, and NW-16 via the Indo-Bangladesh Protocol (IBP) route by Inland & Coastal Shipping Limited (ICSL). Approved at a budget of Rs. 95.42 Crore for 3 years. Tonnage Tax Extension: Announced in the Union Budget on 01.02.2025, extending the special taxation system under the Indian Vessels Act, 2021 to inland vessels operating on NWs, rivers, and canals. Tax is calculated based on vessel size (tonnage) rather than net profit, ensuring stable, predictable, and lower tax burden. National Waterways Regulations 2025: Notified to provide a transparent regulatory framework that encourages private sector capital investment in building and operating inland waterways terminals and jetties. Cargo Aggregation & MMLPs: To resolve multimodality challenges arising from lack of industrial concentration along river banks, Multi-Modal Logistics Parks (MMLP) at Varanasi and Integrated Cluster-cum-Logistics Park at Sahibganj are being developed through NHLML (MoRTH). Rail connectivity to 3 MMTs is assigned to M/s Indian Port and Rail Company Ltd. PSU Cargo Shift Mandate: Over 140 Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) across key ministries (Petroleum & Natural Gas, Co-operation, Fertilizer, Food & Public Distribution, Heavy Industries, Steel, and Coal) have been engaged to mandate cargo allocation and modal shift to waterways. The Coastal Shipping Act, 2025: Enacted to modernize regulation at par with international standards, expand vessel chartering entities, reduce compliance burdens, and foster ease of doing business. Effective from 15.03.2026. Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme: Announced in Union Budget 2026–27 to increase the share of Inland Waterways and Coastal Shipping from 6% to 12% by 2047. IBP Route Operationalization: Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route No. 5 & 6 between Maia and Sultanganj has been operationalized with successful trial movements. REGIONAL WATERWAYS DEVELOPMENT & NATIONWIDE STATUS Northeast Region (NER) Waterways (NW-2 & NW-16) In addition to completed works (MMLP Jogighopa terminal, Bogibeel cargo-cum-tourist terminal, Dhubri & Bogibeel customs/immigration buildings, and NH-27 approach road), key ongoing projects include: Fairway development via Dredging Corporation of India (DCI) on NW-2 (Rs. 143 Crore). Ship Repair Facility at Pandu (revised cost Rs. 283 Crore). Tourist Jetty at Bishwanath Ghat & Cargo-cum-Cruise Terminal at Neamati Ghat (Rs. 158 Crore). Regional Centre of Excellence at Dibrugarh (Rs. 188 Crore). Steel Gangway with Yoke System at Pandu (Rs. 2.88 Crore). Regional Office, MSDC, Guest House & ITAT building at Fancy Bazar (Rs. 50.00 Crore). Link Road connecting Pandu Terminal with Ship Repair Facility (Rs. 55 Crore). 2 Steel Pontoons (Rs. 3.40 Crore) and 2 SDB Vessels (Rs. 2.88 Crore) for NW-2. Mathematical Modelling of Bogibe

evaluation.reason: The news details the development of inland waterways, logistics cost reduction, policy measures like the Jalvahak Scheme, and integration with the PM Gati Shakti Master Plan, which are vital topics for the economy and infrastructure sections of the UPSC syllabus.

articles.title: Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme
articles.description: PIB Backgrounder Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme Catalysing Rural Economies through Grassroots Entrepreneurship प्रविष्टि तिथि: 25 JUL 2026 10:12AM by PIB Delhi The Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme supports non-farm enterprises through training, finance, mentoring, and community-led institutional support. By June 30, 2026, SVEP had supported 4.32 lakh rural enterprises across the country. The programme has strongly focused on social inclusion and equitable access to entrepreneurship opportunities. Around 86% of entrepreneurs belong to SC, ST, Minority, and OBC communities. Through SHGs, CRP-EPs, bank linkages, and convergence with schemes like Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, SVEP has expanded its outreach. SVEP has emerged as an effective grassroots model for poverty reduction, local employment generation, and rural economic development. Enterprise-Led Rural Transformation in India India has the third-largest start-up ecosystem in the world. It has thrived with the support of favourable government policies and has proven highly beneficial for the economy's growth. However, most of the Indian start-up ecosystems are based in urban areas. Hence, the government has launched several initiatives to promote entrepreneurship and innovation in rural areas. One of the key initiatives is the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP). Launched in 2016, SVEP is a sub-scheme of the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). The programme supports Self Help Groups (SHGs) and their family members in establishing small enterprises in the non-farm sector. It provides financial assistance, institutional support, business management training, soft skill development, and business development services. This promotes sustainable livelihoods and self-employment opportunities in rural areas. SVEP also facilitates access to banking linkages and convergence with government schemes. The strategic focus has been on achieving long-term economic growth and wider social benefits. A key feature of SVEP has been community-based decision-making for funding and supporting enterprises locally. Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission The Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana–National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM) is one of the world’s largest livelihood initiatives. It mobilizes rural poor households into Self-Help Groups (SHGs), predominantly women. The focus is on providing them with sustainable livelihoods, access to financial services, and skill development. As of mid-June 2026, more than 10.29 crore rural households have been mobilized into SHGs under DAY-NRLM. Scaling Rural Entrepreneurship Across India SVEP has adopted an all-inclusive approach, with a strong focus on supporting women, marginalized communities, and individuals with limited educational attainment. Since its inception till June 15, 2026, the programme has supported over 4.32 lakh rural enterprises. Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh have recorded the highest number of enterprises supported under the programme. From SHG Member to Rural Business Leader Ms. Bhagyashri Londhe from Jahanpur, Maharashtra, began her journey by joining an SHG in 2014. Participation in SHG and Village Organization (VOs) activities strengthened her leadership and business skills. She began her entrepreneurial journey by producing small-scale quantities of masala, papad, and pickles. A ₹45,000 Community Enterprise Fund loan under SVEP enabled her to scale up production by leveraging locally sourced raw materials. Her entrepreneurial efforts gained recognition at Mahalaxmi Saras 2019-20, where she earned ₹5 lakh in revenue within ten days. Her aspirations to learn and grow enabled her to upgrade her business knowledge and skills. She completed her Class 10 education through an open university while managing her enterprise. Training under NRLM and Krishi Vigyan Kendra enhanced her business literacy and technical capabilities. Consequently, her enterprise started producing large volumes daily, generating regular income, and creating employment for rural women. Her journey demonstrates how entrepreneurship, continuous learning, and institutional support can transform aspiring women into successful business leaders. To support the continued expansion of SVEP, the government has released a cumulative central share of ₹942.09 crore up to February 2026. This is nearly 738% higher than the cumulative ₹112.39 crore released between the programme's launch in 2016 and January 2018. Roadmap for Nurturing and Scaling Rural Enterprises SVEP is implemented through the State Rural Livelihoods Missions (SRLMs), with a provision of ₹6.50 crore per block and an average investment of ₹27,083 per enterprise. At the block level, Block Resource Centres–Enterprise Promotion (BRC-EPs) coordinate programme implementation. Trained Community Resource Persons–Enterprise Promotion (CRP-EPs) provide technical assistance to the Block Resource Centres on enterprise promotion. Banks extend financial support to eligible entrepreneurs. Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and their federations help identify potential entrepreneurs. Community institutions facilitate enterprise establishment and provide handholding support. They also manage loans through the Community Enterprise Fund (CEF). Community institutions also regularly monitor enterprise performance and growth. Digital tools support business planning, loan appraisal, and enterprise tracking. This integrated mechanism ensures effective implementation and enterprise development. CRP-EPs are selected jointly by SRLMs and Project Implementing Agencies through testing, training, and certification. Preference is given to local residents with basic business and mathematical skills. At least 90% of CRP-EPs are selected from SHG households, with women constituting a minimum of 60% of the cadre. Each CRP-EP provides mentoring, training, and credit facilitation support to up to 50

evaluation.reason: The news details the progress, funding, and implementation mechanism of the Start-up Village Entrepreneurship Programme (SVEP), a sub-scheme of DAY-NRLM, which is directly relevant to inclusive economic growth, rural development, and poverty alleviation.

articles.title: Two Days of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 successfully concluded at IIT Hyderabad with focus on AI for Sustainability and Global South Cooperation
articles.description: Ministry of Science & Technology Two Days of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 successfully concluded at IIT Hyderabad with focus on AI for Sustainability and Global South Cooperation Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 7:32PM by PIB Delhi The Day 01 of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 with the focal theme “Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Sustainable Development and Strengthening Global South Cooperation” commenced today at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Hyderabad, bringing together member and participating countries from BRICS to deliberate on the 3C’s Collective, Collaborative and Context sensitive approaches towards Artificial Intelligence (AI). The forum witnessed the presence of 08 BRICS member countries - Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Russia and South Africa along with 05 BRICS partner countries - Nigeria, Vietnam, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Malaysia. Delivering the Presidential Address of the host academy - Indian National Science Academy (INSA), Prof. Shekhar Mande, President of INSA, underscored the transformative role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in addressing priority global and global south challenges, and also emphasized the importance of ensuring that AI systems remain ethical, inclusive, transparent and accessible to all socio-economic fabric of the society. Dr. Debashis Mitra, Vice President (International Affairs), INSA delivered the context-setting address, underlining the urgency for strengthened multilateral scientific engagement. This was followed by an institutional address by Prof. B. S. Murty, Director of IIT Hyderabad who focussed on the various AI associated programmes undertaken at IIT Hyderabad. Key Focus Areas of AI Collaboration The deliberations identified five priority verticals for AI-driven interventions: Advanced Materials and Manufacturing: Accelerating materials discovery, enabling smart manufacturing and optimizing supply chains. Healthcare: Enhancing clinical decision-making, enabling population-scale screening and advancing health research. Climate Change and Environmental Sustainability: Improving long-term forecasting, integrating AI with physical models and enabling risk mitigation. Agriculture and Food Security: Providing AI-powered advisories, accelerating seed research and leveraging digital public infrastructure. Disaster Prediction and Management: Strengthening forecasting capabilities, seismic analysis and resource optimization during emergencies. The thematic focus of the Forum was introduced in the Statement Overview session led by Prof. Ambuj Sagar, IIT Delhi and set the stage for detailed deliberations. Representatives from participating academies presented their national perspectives and engaged in substantive discussions. Brazilian Academy of Sciences emphasized inclusive AI for healthcare, climate resilience and food security Chinese Academy of Sciences highlighted data sharing, validation and evidence-based policymaking aligned with SDGs. Academy of Scientific Research and Technology, Egypt called for capacity building and a BRICS AI Network Ethiopian Academy of Sciences stressed preservation of linguistic diversity alongside cybersecurity and AI education. Indonesian Academy of Sciences underlined explainability, ethical risks and the need for AI to augment human judgement. Russian Academy of Sciences advocated trusted AI systems with strong ethics, transparency and institutional mechanisms such as Centres of Excellence. Academy of Science of South Africa focused on addressing the digital divide and prioritizing climate, health and food security. The Nigerian Academy of Science emphasized ethical AI and data-driven planning. Vietnam Academy of Science and Technology raised concerns on employment, local data and environmental impacts. National Academy of Sciences of Belarus highlighted telemedicine and data security National Academy of Sciences of the Republic of Kazakhstan stressed technology access, SDG alignment and support for young scientists. Summarizing the deliberations, Prof. U. B. Desai, Vice President (Fellowship Affairs), INSA highlighted the need for enhanced cooperation, capacity building and knowledge exchange among member countries. The day also featured a Plenary Lecture by Prof. Anurag Agrawal, Vice President (Science Policy), INSA on the topic “Why AI in healthcare? (And When Not to Use It).” The formal proceedings of Day 01 concluded with discussions, followed by a cultural programme and networking dinner. The second day of the BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 concluded initiated with a plenary lecture by Prof. Indranil Manna, Vice President (Science & Society), INSA. He highlighted the role of AI in materials discovery, including data collection, pattern extraction, physics-based modelling and identification of promising material candidates. The keynote lecture by Dr. Ashish Lele, Director, CSIR-NCL, focused on “Harnessing AI and Green Hydrogen: Driving Efficiency and Decarbonization.” He outlined India’s energy transition pathway, the importance of the National Green Hydrogen Mission and the need for greener logistics and decarbonized data centres. A key highlight of the concluding day was the Open Discussion on the Joint Statement, chaired by Prof. Shekhar C. Mande, President, INSA, where representatives from BRICS member and partner science academies engaged in extensive deliberations to finalize a consensus communiqué. The Joint Statement, reflecting the shared vision and recommendations of the participating academies, is expected to be endorsed within a week and will be presented at the forthcoming BRICS Science, Technology and Innovation (STI) Ministerial Meeting in August 2026. In his concluding remarks, Shri Shambhulingappa Hakki, Joint Secretary (MER & G20) and BRICS Sous Sherpa emphasized that science is an indispensable pillar of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and evidence-based public policy. Congratulating the participating academies f

evaluation.reason: The BRICS Science Academies Forum Meeting 2026 highlights multilateral scientific engagement, Global South cooperation, and AI governance, which are crucial topics for international relations and science policy in the UPSC syllabus.

articles.title: Union Environment Minister reviews Haryana's Air Pollution Action Plan with Chief Minister (Haryana)
articles.description: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change Union Environment Minister reviews Haryana's Air Pollution Action Plan with Chief Minister (Haryana) Shri Bhupender Yadav stresses Strict Enforcement, Accelerated Implementation and Whole-of-Society approach to curb NCR Air Pollution in a time-bound manner Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 10:21PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today held a comprehensive review meeting with the Chief Minister of Haryana, Shri Nayab Singh Saini, and senior officials of the State Government to assess the progress of ongoing measures aimed at improving air quality in Delhi-NCR. During the meeting, the Minister emphasized the need for accelerated implementation, stronger inter-agency coordination and strict enforcement to ensure substantial reduction in pollution levels before the onset of the winter season. Haryana Minister for Environment and Forest, Shri Rao Narbir Singh, was also present during the meeting. Emphasizing the urgency of timely action, Shri Bhupender Yadav said, "The window before the winter season must be fully utilized to implement pollution control measures in mission mode. Timely execution, effective coordination and strict enforcement will be critical to achieving visible improvements in Delhi-NCR's air quality." Reviewing measures to curb Road Dust, the Minister requested that end-to-end paving and greening of roads with local species shrubs/grasses during monsoons be undertaken on priority, with focused attention on pothole identification and repair, construction of footpaths and pavements, roadside greening and deep cleaning of roads. Shri Yadav requested that all gaps in the deployment of Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) be bridged by September this year. He further suggested that all MRSMs be geo-tagged to facilitate real-time monitoring of road-cleaning operations and improve accountability. Reviewing the status of Electric Mobility, the Minister stressed that deployment of electric buses across the NCR municipal corporations in Haryana should be expedited, noting significant gaps in the existing fleet. He congratulated the Haryana Government for the rapid installation of EV charging stations across the seven municipal corporation areas under review. On the issue of End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, Shri Yadav requested the authorities to expedite issuance of No Objection Certificates (NOCs) for transfer of eligible EoL vehicles outside the NCR, while simultaneously encouraging scientific scrapping of old and unfit vehicles. He also called for faster replacement of old polluting vehicles with electric vehicles under the Parivartan Scheme. The Minister requested that Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) cameras be installed at all fuel stations for effective implementation of the "No PUCC, No Fuel" initiative. Stressing the need to improve urban traffic management, Shri Yadav asked the authorities to identify Traffic Congestion Hotspots on a mission mode and implement suitable mitigation measures at the earliest. Reviewing Industrial Pollution control measures, Shri Yadav stressed the need for accelerated installation of Online Continuous Emission Monitoring Systems (OCEMS) and Air Pollution Control Devices (APCDs) across industrial units. The Minister reviewed progress on Construction And Demolition Waste management and requested that establishment of Secondary Collection Centres for C&D waste be expedited. He also stressed that liquidation of Legacy Waste should be undertaken on a war footing. Referring to municipal solid waste (MSW) and Biomass Burning, Shri Yadav called for the constitution of dedicated task forces and emphasized achieving 100 per cent collection of municipal solid waste and biomass to eliminate littering and prevent open burning. On Stubble Burning, Shri Yadav requested the State Government to bridge gaps in procurement of Crop Residue Management (CRM) machinery and accelerate establishment of Custom Hiring Centres. He emphasized the need for intensive Information, Education and Communication (IEC) campaigns and farmer training programmes to promote effective use of CRM equipment. The Minister suggested that local elected representatives identify stubble-burning hotspots in coordination with Gram Panchayats. He further requested District Collectors to survey industrial units and document their crop residue storage and consumption capacities to facilitate efficient demand-supply management. The State authorities were also advised to ensure adequate availability of crop residue balers. Underscoring the importance of public participation and coordinated institutional action, Shri Yadav said, "Air pollution can be effectively tackled only through a 'Whole of Government' and 'Whole of Society' approach". Chief Minister (Haryana), Shri Saini, directed State Government officials for timely action on different measures discussed during the meeting. He thanked the Union Minister for his valuable guidance in this matter. The meeting was attended by the Secretary, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change; Chairperson, Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM); senior officers of the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and the Government of Haryana. Senior officials from the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) and the Haryana State Pollution Control Board (HSPCB) were also present. ***** VM (Release ID: 2289250)

evaluation.reason: The news discusses high-level administrative reviews and strategic measures to curb air pollution in the Delhi-NCR region, covering key environmental issues such as stubble burning, vehicular emissions, and waste management, which are vital for UPSC CSE preparation.

articles.title: Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman outlines 5Rs of responsive tax governance; Calls for greater tax certainty and reduced litigation at the 167th Income Tax celebrations in New Delhi today
articles.description: Ministry of Finance Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman outlines 5Rs of responsive tax governance; Calls for greater tax certainty and reduced litigation at the 167th Income Tax celebrations in New Delhi today The Union Finance Minister reiterates fair, efficient, transparent and taxpayer-centric administrationIncome-tax Act, 2025 and new rules and forms mark landmark reforms towards simpler and taxpayer-friendly tax system: Revenue Secretary Shri Arvind ShrivastavaCBDT Chairman Ravi Agarwal highlights progress in faster return processing, grievance redressal and litigation reductionCBDT advances technology-led tax administration through PAN 2.0, ITBA 2.0, IEC 3.0 and SAKSHAM NUDGEFM Smt. Sitharaman releases six publications highlighting India's growing leadership in international taxation and taxpayer-centric governance Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 9:23PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs Smt. Nirmala Sitharaman participated in the 167th anniversary of Income Tax Day celebrations by Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) in New Delhi today. Shri Arvind Srivastava, Secretary, D/o Revenue; Shri Ravi Agrawal, Chairman, CBDT; Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC: Members of CBDT and CBIC and other senior officers and officials of the Department were present on the occasion. Addressing the 167th Income Tax Day celebrations, Union Finance Minister Smt. Sitharaman emphasised that the role of the Income Tax Department has evolved from tax collection to building a fair, efficient, transparent and taxpayer-centric tax administration. She described the implementation of the Income-tax Act, 2025 as a landmark reform that has simplified the law, reduced compliance costs and strengthened ease of doing business. She also highlighted the enhanced capacity of the e-Filing portal, improved return processing, prompt refunds and significant progress in grievance redressal, while stressing that the Department must move beyond disposal of grievances to analysing recurring issues and preventing them through systemic improvements. She outlined the 5Rs of Responsive Tax Governance - Recognise, Respond, Redress, Reflect and Reform, as guiding principles for taxpayer service, emphasising that honest taxpayers should experience convenience, opportunities to correct bona fide errors and a tax administration that exercises its authority with humility. Stressing that taxpayers are partners in India's development, she called for a continued focus on reducing litigation by strengthening tax certainty. FM Smt. Sitharaman also underlined the importance of strengthening institutional capacity through modern infrastructure, technology and continuous investment in human capital. She appreciated the progress made in upgrading offices and welfare facilities and called for greater capacity building in emerging areas such as artificial intelligence, data analytics, forensic accounting, international taxation, transfer pricing, digital assets, cybersecurity and leadership development. She urged the Department to deepen voluntary compliance, further simplify the taxpayer experience, strengthen tax certainty, harness technology responsibly, build institutional excellence, reinforce public trust and embrace continuous improvement. Congratulating the officers and staff of the Income Tax Department on the occasion of the 167th Income Tax Day, she expressed confidence that the Department would continue to play a pivotal role in promoting ease of doing business, strengthening taxpayer confidence and supporting India's economic growth. In his address on the occasion, Shri Arvind Shrivastava, Secretary, D/o Revenue, Ministry of Finance, extended his greetings to the officers and officials of the Income Tax Department and described the implementation of the Income-tax Act, 2025 and the new Income-tax Rules and Forms as landmark reforms towards a simpler, clearer and more taxpayer-friendly tax system, and appreciated the Department's efforts in strengthening taxpayer outreach, grievance redressal, litigation management and technology-driven service delivery. Emphasising the need to leverage technology while keeping taxpayers at the centre of reforms, he called for continued focus on ease of compliance, tax certainty, quality service delivery and innovation, and expressed confidence that the Department would continue to strengthen public trust and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047. Welcoming the dignitaries on behalf of the Income Tax Department, Shri Ravi Agrawal, recalled the priorities set out by the Union Finance Minister during the previous Income Tax Day celebrations and the expectations articulated at the PRARAMBH programme earlier this year, he outlined the Department's progress over the past year in translating those directions into measurable outcomes. He highlighted the Department's sustained efforts towards reducing litigation, faster disposal of appeals and enhancing tax certainty through Advance Pricing Agreements. He also noted the achievements in the areas of expeditious return processing, appeal-effect orders and refunds, and strengthening grievance redressal. He further highlighted the Department's achievements in expanding taxpayer outreach through initiatives such as PRARAMBH and Samvaad. He also underscored the Department's continued focus on leveraging technology through initiatives such as PAN 2.0, ITBA 2.0, IEC 3.0, Kar Saathi and the SAKSHAM NUDGE framework to simplify compliance, improve taxpayer experience and strengthen voluntary compliance. He expressed his appreciation to all CBDT verticals, including the Exemptions vertical, and the officers involved in framing the Rules and Forms under the Income-tax Act, 2025. Expressing gratitude for the continued guidance and support of the Hon'ble Finance Minister, he reaffirmed the Department's commitment to building a fair, transparent and trusted tax administration through innovation, collaboration a

evaluation.reason: The news outlines significant tax governance reforms, the 5Rs of responsive tax administration, reduction of litigation, and technological advancements by the CBDT, which are highly relevant for the Indian economy and fiscal policy.

articles.title: Department of Telecommunications Activates Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) in Affected Districts of Nagaland, Gujarat, UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu amid Heavy Rainfall and Flooding
articles.description: Ministry of Communications Department of Telecommunications Activates Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) in Affected Districts of Nagaland, Gujarat, UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu amid Heavy Rainfall and Flooding Swift measures taken to ensure uninterrupted telecom connectivity and support emergency operations across disaster-affected region Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has taken immediate and proactive measures to ensure the continuity of essential communication services across disaster-affected regions in Nagaland, Gujarat and the Union Territory of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu. Continuous heavy rainfall, landslides, flash floods, and severe inundation have caused extensive damage to critical telecom infrastructure, leading to large-scale network outages and disrupted transmission routes in these areas. To mitigate communication breakdowns during rescue and relief operations, DoT has invoked emergency response mechanisms under the Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)-2020 for Telecom Services in Response to Disasters and the Unified Licence provisions: Nagaland (Longleng District): Following incessant rainfall, landslides, and multiple Optical Fiber Cable (OFC) cuts, Longleng becomes the second district in Nagaland after Mon to have ICR activated. Directions have been issued to activate ICR immediately upto 23:59 hrs of 27th July, 2026 or till further instructions, whichever is earlier. Valsad district of Gujarat, Dadra & Nagar Haveli district and Daman district of UT: Severe flooding has caused major node outages across Dadra & Nagar Haveli, Daman, and adjoining Valsad district. DoT has authorized immediate activation of ICR Immediately upto 23:59 hrs of 27th July, 2026 or till further instructions, whichever is earlier. The activation of ICR enables mobile subscribers of any provider as well as visiting in-roamers to seamlessly access any available network in locations where their home network is temporarily offline. This ensures optimal utilization of surviving telecom infrastructure and maintains vital connectivity for affected residents, emergency responders, healthcare personnel, and disaster management agencies. The Department of Telecommunications is continuously monitoring network status through its field units and working with all service providers to expedite full restoration of communication networks in the affected districts. What is ICR & how to use it: Intra Circle Roaming (ICR) is a telecom arrangement where a mobile subscriber connects to another operator’s network within the same telecom circle (region). This allows users to access mobile services even if their own operator has no coverage in that specific area. It plays a critical role during natural disasters when mobile infrastructure is damaged. During the time of disaster, if mobile infrastructure is damaged in a region, DoT issues instructions to Telecom Service Operators to implement ICR. To ensure ICR works: Keep "Automatic Network Selection" enabled in your phone settings. If automatic connection fails; Go to Settings>Mobile Networks>Network Operators Manually select another available network ***** NJ/AR (Release ID: 2289168)

evaluation.reason: The activation of Intra-Circle Roaming (ICR) by the Department of Telecommunications during disasters highlights crucial disaster management and telecom infrastructure resilience, which is important for Prelims and GS-3.

articles.title: Five Senior Citizen Homes Inaugurated Across Five States; MoU Signed to Strengthen Elderly Welfare; Innovative Programmes Promote Inter-generational Bonding
articles.description: Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Five Senior Citizen Homes Inaugurated Across Five States; MoU Signed to Strengthen Elderly Welfare; Innovative Programmes Promote Inter-generational Bonding Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi The government continues to strengthen its commitment towards ensuring the dignity, security and well-being of senior citizens through comprehensive initiatives under the Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY). Commemorating the International Day of Older Persons (IDOP) 2025, the Department organised a series of nationwide programmes to promote healthy ageing, social inclusion, legal awareness and inter-generational bonding among senior citizens. This information was given by Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment Shri B.L. Verma in a written reply to Dr. Ashok Kumar Mittal in the Lok Sabha. The nationwide celebrations highlighted the Government's sustained efforts to create an age-friendly society while encouraging active participation of senior citizens in community life. The initiatives also complemented the objectives of AVYAY by strengthening partnerships with institutions, civil society organisations and local communities. As part of the celebrations, a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was signed with the Birla Open Minds Foundation to promote collaborative initiatives for the welfare and empowerment of senior citizens. The Department also virtually inaugurated five Senior Citizen Homes located in Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Assam, Uttar Pradesh and Jharkhand, further expanding institutional care and support infrastructure for elderly citizens across the country. To encourage stronger family values and inter-generational engagement, the Department launched "Naitik Patham", an interactive educational game designed to promote meaningful interaction between younger and older generations. A QR Code-based initiative for Grandparents-Teachers Meetings was also introduced to foster greater involvement of senior citizens in children's educational development. The celebrations included inter-generational bonding programmes in Jabalpur, Badaun, Chhatarpur, Navgaon, Biaora and Mount Abu, bringing together youth and senior citizens through interactive activities. In collaboration with S-VYASA, Bengaluru, yoga sessions and health camps were organised to promote healthy and active ageing among elderly citizens. Recognising the importance of legal awareness, a special session on the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007 was organised in collaboration with the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA). The programme focused on creating awareness regarding the legal rights, welfare provisions and social security measures available to senior citizens while encouraging families and communities to fulfil their responsibilities towards elderly members. A cultural programme titled "Aradhana" was also organised to celebrate the invaluable contribution of senior citizens to society and to encourage their active participation in cultural and community life. Through these initiatives, the Government reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring that every senior citizen lives with dignity, respect, security and access to quality care. Under the umbrella of Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY), the Ministry continues to work in convergence with State Governments, autonomous bodies and civil society organisations to build an inclusive and supportive ecosystem for senior citizens across the country. *** PR – 031 – TAR/KV/GA (Release ID: 2289125)

articles.title: 'Weaves of India' Festival Showcases India's Finest Handloom Heritage at Central Cottage Industries Emporium
articles.description: Ministry of Textiles 'Weaves of India' Festival Showcases India's Finest Handloom Heritage at Central Cottage Industries Emporium The festival is open to visitors from 24 July to 7 August 2026 Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 7:24PM by PIB Delhi The Office of the Development Commissioner (Handlooms), Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, is organizing the 'Weaves of India' Festival at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium (CCIE), Janpath, New Delhi. The festival will remain open to the public from 24 July to 7 August 2026 as part of the celebrations leading up to 12thNational Handloom Day on 7th of August. The festival presents a curated celebration of India's rich and diverse handloom traditions, bringing together exemplary handwoven creations representing 116 heritage weaves from across the country. It offers visitors an opportunity to experience the extraordinary craftsmanship, artistic excellence and cultural legacy preserved by generations of Indian weavers. The exhibition features celebrated weaving traditions from Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Manipur, Chhattisgarh, Bihar, Telangana, Gujarat, Jammu & Kashmir and Tripura, among others. Visitors can explore iconic handloom traditions including Banarasi, Jamdani, Kanchipuram Silk, SambalpuriIkat, Paithani, Kani Pashmina, BawanButi, Kotpad, Ilkal,Kasargod, Himroo and Risha, each representing the unique cultural identity and textile heritage of its region. Beyond showcasing exceptional textiles, the festival aims to strengthen public appreciation for authentic handwoven products while creating greater awareness about sustainable, ethical and artisan-led production systems. It also provides a valuable platform for interaction between master weavers, designers, collectors, buyers, researchers and the general public. The Government of India remains committed to preserving, promoting and revitalising the country's rich handloom heritage through sustained support for artisans, design innovation, market development and consumer awareness. The 'Weaves of India' Festival reflects this commitment by celebrating India's living textile traditions and encouraging citizens to support the country's handloom artisans. The festival is open to visitors at the Central Cottage Industries Emporium, Janpath, New Delhi, from 24 July to 7 August 2026. Members of the public are invited to witness the timeless elegance and unparalleled artistry of India's handwoven heritage. ****** MAM/VN (Release ID: 2289127)

evaluation.reason: The news highlights India's rich handloom heritage, GI-tagged and traditional textile weaves from various states, showcasing Indian art and culture relevant for GS-1.

rejectedArticles.title: BUCHAREST UNIVERSTY OF ECONOMIC STUDIES CONFERS HONORARY DOCTORATE ON THE PRESIDENT
rejectedArticles.description: President's Secretariat BUCHAREST UNIVERSTY OF ECONOMIC STUDIES CONFERS HONORARY DOCTORATE ON THE PRESIDENT DEEPEN COOPERATION THROUGH JOINT RESEARCH AND FACULITY AND STUDENT EXCHANGES: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU TO ROMANIAN UNIVERSITIES Posted On: 24 JUL 2026 11:01PM by PIB Delhi The Bucharest University of Economic Studies conferred an Honorary Doctorate on the President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, at a ceremony held in Bucharest, Romania today (July 24, 2026). In her acceptance address, the President thanked the Rector, Senate and entire university community of the Bucharest University of Economic Studies for this recognition. She accepted the honour as a reflection of the enduring friendship between the peoples of India and Romania. The President said that education has been the single most transformative force in her life. She stated that she had the privilege of working as a teacher and experienced first-hand how a single classroom, however modest, can change a family's future, and also whole community's future in course of time. She underlined that education is not merely a means of individual advancement, but the foundation of a just and inclusive society. The President said that the friendship between India and Romania is based on mutual respect, trust and shared democratic values. Education has been one of the strongest pillars of this partnership. For decades, Romanian Universities have welcomed Indian students, particularly in medicine, engineering and technology. She urged the Bucharest University of Economic Studies and other Romanian educational institutions to deepen cooperation through joint research and faculty and student exchanges. The President said that today, as the world is being reshaped by artificial intelligence, digital technologies and other rapid scientific advances, universities like the Bucharest University of Economic Studies have even greater responsibility to ensure that wisdom, ethics and compassion guide knowledge. The President told students that they are the architects of tomorrow's world. Success is measured not only by professional achievement, but also by the values they uphold and the positive difference they make in the lives of others. She advised them to remain curious in their pursuit of knowledge, confident in their abilities and compassionate in their actions. She urged them to use their talents to build bridges across cultures and contribute to a more peaceful and prosperous world. The Bucharest University of Economic Studies is Romania's foremost institution for higher education in economics, business and public administration. Established in 1913, it was the first university in Romania dedicated exclusively to economic sciences and has since educated generations of economists, policymakers, business leaders and public administrators. The Doctor Honoris Causa is the university's highest academic distinction, awarded to eminent personalities for exceptional contributions to academia, public service and international cooperation. Please click here to see the President’s Speech *** MJPS/SS/PRK (Release ID: 2289265)
